newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hang Seng Bank tumbles after recent surge.
newsitem.headline: Hang Seng Bank tumbles after recent surge.

text.p: Shares in Hang Seng Bank Ltd tumbled on Monday as investors locked in profits following Friday's surge into record territory, brokers said.
The stock shed HK$5.00 to HK$104.50 after breaking above HK$100.00 for the first time on Friday to an all-time high of HK$110.00 on speculation a Chinese company would buy a stake in the bank.
"It is obvious that the stock is going to run into profit-taking," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities.
"There is some rotation into Bank of East Asia," he added.
Shares in Bank of East Asia Ltd jumped HK$1.60 to HK$31.60.
Brokers said China may also be interested in buying a stake in the bank.
"Buying interest has switched to Bank of East Asia since it is one of the largest local banks following Hang Seng Bank," said Anthony Mak, a sales director at Vickers Ballas.
But Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities, said China was unlikely to buy a stake in Hang Seng Bank, a subsidiary of index heavyweight HSBC Holdings Plc .
"It would cost a lot of money and I don't think the Chinese government would spend that much," he said. "Also, I don't think Hongkong Bank will sell because they don't need the money."
Shares in HSBC fell HK$1.00 to HK$232.00.
